Vardzia and Borjomi — the Southern Route

Two days in Samtskhe-Javakheti: Borjomi park, Rabati castle, Khertvisi and the cave city of Vardzia.

days
2 / 1 nights
Total distance
550 km
Total driving
9:00
Car needed
Economy class
Season
All year
Difficulty
Moderate

Click a marker for details. Coloured lines are ready-made road trips.

This is the southern direction — the Mtkvari valley, which leads out of Tbilisi through Borjomi and Akhaltsikhe and ends close to the Turkish border at the rock-cut city of Vardzia. All 265 kilometres are asphalt, so an economy car reaches the end comfortably, although the final stretch narrows and winds along the gorge.

Day one is the climb from the plain into the mountains. Borjomi is a nineteenth-century spa town where you drink the famous mineral water straight from the spring in the central park. Then the valley tightens and Akhaltsikhe appears with Rabati Castle, a rebuilt citadel that holds a mosque, a church, a synagogue and the old fortress towers inside a single wall. Day two continues south: Khertvisi Fortress guards the confluence of two rivers, and then comes Vardzia itself — a twelfth-century monastery carved into the cliff under Queen Tamar, thirteen storeys deep, with hundreds of chambers and the frescoed Church of the Dormition at its heart.

The route suits travellers who care about history and architecture: in two days you cover two millennia. Respect the distances, though — you spend over four hours a day behind the wheel, so the overnight in Akhaltsikhe or near Vardzia is not optional. Doing it as a day trip means 530 kilometres in one go. The road stays open in winter, but the Javakheti plateau is genuinely cold.

Day-by-day plan

Day 1 · Tbilisi → Borjomi → Akhaltsikhe (205 km, 3 h 20 min) - 08:30 Leave Tbilisi on the E60 via Gori and Khashuri. - 11:00 Borjomi Central Park, the mineral spring and the cable car (2 h). - 13:30 Lunch in Borjomi (1 h). - 15:00 The Mtkvari gorge towards Akhaltsikhe, stop at Atskuri (30 min). - 16:30 Rabati Castle in Akhaltsikhe — upper citadel, mosque and museum (2 h). - Overnight in Akhaltsikhe.

Day 2 · Akhaltsikhe → Vardzia → Tbilisi (345 km, 5 h 40 min) - 09:00 Set off towards Aspindza along the river. - 10:00 Khertvisi Fortress at the confluence (45 min). - 11:15 Vardzia — the cave city, the church and its frescoes (2 h 30 min). - 14:00 Lunch near Vardzia or in Aspindza (1 h). - 15:30 Drive back via Akhaltsikhe and Borjomi. - 21:00 Back in Tbilisi.

Stops on this route

Spa resort

Borjomi Central Park and Mineral Springs

Fortress

Rabati Castle (Akhaltsikhe)

A restored fortress-town in the heart of Akhaltsikhe where a mosque, a church and a synagogue share one courtyard.

2 h
Fortress

Khertvisi Fortress

One of the oldest fortresses in Georgia, standing where two rivers meet on the road to Vardzia.

A 12th-century cave city and monastery cut into the Mtkvari gorge, the flagship monument of Queen Tamar's era.

3 h

Tips

  • Fill the tank in Akhaltsikhe — stations are rare beyond Aspindza.
  • Vardzia means many stairs and narrow tunnels: wear proper shoes and bring a small torch.
  • In summer Vardzia bakes in full sun — go early morning or after 16:00, with water and a hat.
  • The Javakheti plateau is cold eight months a year; winter tyres are mandatory in the cold season.
  • Vardzia and back in one day is 530 km — the overnight in Akhaltsikhe makes the trip far more pleasant.
